evidence: action.ts imported `PreviewRows` from layout-preview.js while layout-preview.ts imported `ActionRuntime` from action.js, a real type-level cycle. c741e2c moved `PreviewSegment`/`PreviewRows` into action.ts beside `ActionRuntime.layout` instead of into node-registry as suggested, and layout-preview now imports one way, which removes the back-edge. guidance_note: When a new type is published on a base module's runtime interface (`ActionRuntime.layout`), define the type in that base module from the start rather than importing it back from the feature module that consumes it.

guidance_note: When adopting a shared constant like `EDIT_NS` in one place (render.ts's `shown`), grep the diff for the literal it replaces (`"edit."`) and switch every occurrence in the same commit, tests included.

guidance_note: When a test title states a structural claim ('row for row'), assert that structure directly (per-row equality), and check it by breaking the code under test in that one dimension before pushing.

narrative: Rounds 0 and 1 were cancelled CoPirate runs with no findings. In round 2, four inline findings plus one out-of-diff summary item landed on ba80281, which was the agent's own follow-up, not a fix. The agent fixed three inline findings in c741e2c, correctly pushed back on the narrow-width edge case, and skipped the out-of-diff stale-comment item. Round 3 raised that same item inline (F5), so round 3 was avoidable. Round 4's two test-rigor findings were on code that predates every review commit, so the review found them late rather than a fix causing them. No finding was caused by a fix.
guidance_observations: The address-pr-reviews pass handled inline threads only and ignored the summary's 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' list, which cost a full review round for a one-paragraph comment fix.
The flags in this PR are all false positives in the fix-caused sense: ba80281 answered no finding, and 64c1156 touched only a comment, so every flagged finding sat on pre-review code.

Two of the round-4 findings were tests whose assertions were weaker than their own titles or comments promised. A pre-push check that every test title's claim is directly asserted would have caught both in the original PR.
